tytul: Pickled eggs: the NCHFP dilled eggs, no curry version
wstep: NCHFP has no recipe for pickled eggs in a curry or turmeric brine, so this card describes the NCHFP recipe for dilled eggs, which are kept only in the refrigerator.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Home pickled eggs stored at room temperature have caused botulism, according to a CDC report.
Never keep pickled eggs at room temperature except when serving, and then for no more than 2 hours in the 40–140 °F (about 4–60 °C) zone.
It is not safe to can pickled eggs at home; all NCHFP pickled egg recipes are for the refrigerator.

akapity: The NCHFP pickled egg recipes are red beet, sweet and sour, dark and spicy, cidered, dilled and pineapple eggs; none of them uses curry or turmeric.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): JarAtlas has no tested source for adding curry, turmeric or other spices outside the recipe, so this card does not give them; do not change the amounts of vinegar, water or salt.
Eggs are a low-acid food (pH 6.4–9.0), and vinegar may not penetrate every part of the egg.
Each NCHFP recipe uses 12 peeled, hard-cooked eggs.
Eggs for pickling should have clean, sound shells; small or medium eggs are usually a good choice, so that the seasoning can penetrate.
The dilled eggs pickling solution is made with 1 1/2 cups of white vinegar, 1 cup of water and 3 teaspoons of salt.

The seasonings are 3/4 teaspoon of dill weed, 1/4 teaspoon of white pepper, 1/4 teaspoon of mustard seed, 1/2 teaspoon of onion juice or minced onion, and 1/2 teaspoon of minced garlic or 1 peeled garlic clove.
Make a pinhole in the large end of each egg, place the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover them with cold water to an inch above the eggs.
Put a lid on the pan, bring the water to a boil, turn down the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Place the eggs in cold water and peel them when cool, starting at the large end; you can peel them under cold running water.
Bring all the ingredients except the eggs to a boil, reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Pack no more than one dozen eggs loosely into a warm, pre-sterilized quart jar, or another container of similar size that can be closed tightly.
There must be plenty of pickling solution, enough to cover the eggs completely.
Pour the hot solution over the eggs, cover the jar and refrigerate it immediately.
Keep the eggs refrigerated at all times.
The eggs must stay completely covered with the pickling solution throughout storage.
Small eggs usually need 1–2 weeks to take up the flavor, and medium or large eggs may need 2–4 weeks.
Use the eggs within 3–4 months for best quality.
